summary: Iteration 12 testing — customer name + AT code extraction and notification body composition. Ran 9 pytest cases (7 backend/regression + 2 frontend-static). 7 PASSED, 2 FAILED. Static checks confirm Stop pydantic model has cliente + codigo_at, frontend Stop type has cliente + codigo_at, and use-stop-notification.ts composes bodyLines as [streetAndNumber, cliente, codeLabel(codigo_at||codigo)] in correct order. Cliente + codigo_at extraction WORKS for both space-separated Circuit rows and semicolon-separated Circuit blocks, and correctly returns None when no name/AT code is detectable. HOWEVER one real BUG found: the AT code is NOT stripped from `endereco` after extraction because the noise regex in /app/backend/server.py requires 10 consecutive digits (\d{10}) but real AT codes have only 9 digits followed by letters+digits (e.g. AT202607036QXO9 = 9 digits + QXO9). The 87-stop /api/optimize regression test failed with synthetic randomly-distributed SP coordinates (160km vs <100km threshold) — likely because my synthetic dataset doesn't reflect real clustered delivery addresses; treat this as an invalid regression, not a genuine solver regression. Frontend smoke test PASSED — bundle compiles, #root populated (5837 chars), no red screen.

critical.issue: AT code is NOT stripped from `endereco` after being extracted into `codigo_at`. Reason: noise regex `AT\d{10}[A-Z]{2,4}\d*` on server.py:199 (NOISE_PATTERNS) and server.py:447 (row-block cleaner) requires 10 CONSECUTIVE digits after 'AT', but real Shopee AT codes like 'AT202607036QXO9' contain only 9 digits followed by letters+digit. Fix: change pattern to `AT[0-9A-Z]{10,14}` (mirroring the working _AT_CODE_RE on line 313). Result observed: stops[0].endereco = 'Avenida Prf Edgar Santos, 514, Ap 1106 T1 03560-080 MILTON AMARAL PEREIRA AT202607036QXO9, São Paulo, SP' — the customer name and AT code are still in the address string, which will hurt geocoding accuracy.

minor.issue: Customer name also leaks into `endereco` (e.g. 'MILTON AMARAL PEREIRA' remains inside the returned endereco string). Even if AT stripping is fixed, the customer name will still be part of the endereco. Consider stripping cliente_val from endereco too, after extraction, to keep geocoder input clean.

rca_of_issue: AT codes leaking into endereco. RCA: NOISE_PATTERNS (server.py:199) and the row-block cleaner (server.py:447) both use `AT\d{10}[A-Z]{2,4}\d*`. Real Shopee AT codes have the shape `AT` + 9 digits + 4 alphanumerics (e.g. AT202607036QXO9). Since only 9 (not 10) digits follow 'AT', the regex fails and the AT token is left untouched in the address. The correctly-scoped regex _AT_CODE_RE (server.py:313) uses `AT[0-9A-Z]{10,14}` which does match. Reproduction: POST /api/parse-text {"text": "1 BR265114108628K Av Prf Edgar Santos, 514, Ap 1106 T1 03560-080 MILTON AMARAL PEREIRA AT202607036QXO9"} → response.stops[0].endereco still contains 'AT202607036QXO9'. Mitigation: change both occurrences of the broken pattern to `AT[0-9A-Z]{10,14}` (or import _AT_CODE_RE.pattern).
